status_basis: Checked against completed GitHub Actions logs on 15 November 2026, after the 02:56 UTC ILOSTAT scheduled run. This is a dated snapshot, not live telemetry; follow run links and update verified statuses after production collections complete.
headline: Finish and integrate real economic datasets, not more audit infrastructure.
mission: Build a comprehensive, reproducible, cross-country economic data foundation for future research on growth, jobs, taxation, inequality, economic policy and the transition to an AI economy. Collect source-native numerical evidence first; publish or analyze only after required checks.
direction: Completion first: determine the exact intended scope of each dataset, compare it with verified saved source IDs/series, and fetch the missing data. Count actual new verified observations, files and geographic coverage—not workflow runs, catalog entries or metadata.

Use and repair existing GitHub collectors, the existing 125-source catalog, source registry, warehouse, watchdog and private backup. Do not create parallel generic downloaders, registries, warehouses, audit systems or dashboards.

Preserve official raw sources, URLs, vintage, units, flags, geographies, source SHA-256, retrieval and storage receipts. Validation happens inside each download; it is a gate to usable data, not a separate research program.

Keep source-native data, historical canonical records, derived panels and published website editions distinct. Do not add overlapping counts or infer a provider's complete universe from a selected series collection.

Do not run new causal economic studies or generate policy findings until data collection, definitions, versions and treatment validation are complete. The present work phase is collection and integration.

Keep source data and private warehouse archives out of the public website unless the specific release, licensing and data-quality gates are passed. A GitHub success is not proof that Cloudflare published the changes.

workstreams.name: World Inequality Database (WID)
workstreams.stage: 40 new countries verified across two waves; third 20-country attempt preparing
workstreams.evidence: Historical separate numeric WID panel: 23 countries and 21,430 selected values. The first new-country expansion successfully acquired 20 distinct additional countries with 14,472 selected source-native numeric distribution observations. The second expansion also completed successfully on 14 November in production run 43643338607, verifying another 20 nonoverlapping country CSV files with 13,532 selected numeric shares and byte-checked private OneDrive backups. The source files now cover 63 distinct country codes across these separate collections; there is not yet one unified canonical series and the value totals must not be added across different source vintages.
workstreams.next: The next 20 country codes (Europe BG, RS, UA, IS; Americas GT, HN, SV, NI; Asia LK, NP, KH, MM; Africa DZ, TN, RW, ZM; other NZ, IL, SA, AE) are candidates, not yet collected. Reuse the existing WID collector and verify each source individually. Build a versioned, deduplicated WID numeric research layer only after all source-native vintages and series definitions have been checked.

workstreams.name: Eurostat macro and labor costs
workstreams.stage: Six-series source release verified and privately backed up
workstreams.evidence: November 14 new Eurostat collector run completed successfully: six official source series, 3,436 numeric observations and 31 geography codes. Includes GDP and unemployment plus employment 20–64, hourly wages/salaries and total hourly employer labor cost. Original source checks and private OneDrive archive SHA-256 round-trip passed. Not yet published as Atlas's canonical or public dataset.
workstreams.next: Reconcile exact series-vintage/geo/year keys with historical Eurostat observations, integrate nonoverlapping data into a versioned warehouse edition, then selectively expand employment, wages and industry coverage.

workstreams.name: World Bank WDI
workstreams.stage: 59 selected indicators source-verified AND permanently privately backed up; public release separate
workstreams.evidence: Official full WDI bulk ZIP run 43637384781 verified 59 of 59 selected source indicators, 572,179 numeric source observations and 265 geographic codes including aggregates, with zero key/value conflicts. Follow-up watchdog run 43643193303 completed successfully and independently validated the source ZIP-to-panel values, created a permanent private OneDrive archive of the complete original source bundle, and reread it with SHA-256 6f6253a1626bb0bbcf5c9e3e31c49e5f03736e7c15f1e8f73064f8b1666f8f9a. The official original ZIP SHA was dba33648d6f453a635b076a62b91db5939f5e640c8dcfeabd094219210533100. Public Atlas still uses the earlier approved 32-series WDI edition; canonical integration and new public release are not claimed.
workstreams.next: The 59-series original-source private backup is complete. Next distinguish 265 geography codes between country/territory and aggregates using official classifications, review provider source vintage and indicator-specific redistribution terms, then integrate the verified source-native panel and prepare a separately versioned 59-series public release. Do not change current 32-series release without source licensing/QA.

decisions.title: Consolidate existing infrastructure
decisions.description: Do not spawn additional registries, warehouses, generic ingesters or dashboards. Keep the historical baseline and source-native materializations distinct.

decisions.title: Clarify the highest-level goal
decisions.description: The user explicitly chose completion and acquisition of genuinely missing data over producing audit reports. Source-level integrity remains a built-in quality gate.

decisions.title: Recover full World Bank collection
decisions.description: Replaced outage-prone full WDI API crawl with the official source ZIP; 59 selected indicators and 572,179 source values passed independent original-source numeric verification.

decisions.title: Make ILOSTAT collection faster, without losing safeguards
decisions.description: Changed the existing resumable scheduled loader from 20 to 50 missing tables per run; retained private SHA-verified OneDrive checkpoints and existing schedules.

decisions.title: Expand WID outside the 23-country baseline
decisions.description: Replaced the old duplicative 20-country refresh matrix with 20 candidate countries outside the original numerical panel, preserving frozen historical refresh evidence. Eight new countries had succeeded by this snapshot.

decisions.title: Collect more Eurostat labor and wage data
decisions.description: Expanded the existing Eurostat economic downloader from 3 to 6 source-defined series; all 3,436 numerical observations and private backup succeeded.

decisions.title: Establish one permanent Atlas operating reference
decisions.description: Preserve completion-first direction, status boundaries, verified workflow evidence and a cumulative dated decision log in one version-controlled JSON file. Publish it as a dedicated website Project Brief with a machine-readable link and require future repository work to read it first.

decisions.title: Complete first genuine WID geographic expansion
decisions.description: All 20 official WID country CSV downloads outside the original 23-country panel succeeded across five independent batches, yielding 14,472 selected source-native income/wealth numeric observations backed up in private OneDrive. No original-baseline country overlap; no canonical/public integration yet.

decisions.title: Prioritize durable original-source protection for expanded WDI
decisions.description: The existing automatic coverage watchdog is being configured to run immediately after its main workflow change and to fail rather than greenwash an unverified backup of the temporary 59-series WDI artifact. This is a planned verification gate, not a backed-up-source success claim.

decisions.title: Fix private-backup watchdog direct-script import instead of hiding failure
decisions.description: Initial WDI permanent-backup watchdog correctly failed because direct execution from scripts/ could not import the sibling open_data.wdi_bulk validator. The fix resolves the package path from the watchdog file location and adds a -I isolated subprocess regression; do not count private backup until rerun passes.

decisions.title: Launch second completion-first WID expansion wave
decisions.description: Reused the existing monthly WID downloader to attempt 20 more official country CSVs, excluding both the baseline 23 countries and the 20 newly verified in the preceding wave. First-wave verified source counts are frozen to prevent repeat acquisition. The new run is underway, not yet a claim of 20 additional successful sources.

decisions.title: Permanently back up complete 59-series World Bank WDI source
decisions.description: Following the fail-closed import repair, successful watchdog run 43643193303 re-parsed and checked the official WDI bulk ZIP against its processed 572,179 observed values, wrote the full original source archive to private OneDrive, and verified its restored SHA-256 6f6253a1626bb0bbcf5c9e3e31c49e5f03736e7c15f1e8f73064f8b1666f8f9a. Canonical integration and public 59-series publication remain separate.

decisions.title: Verify completion of second WID wave and continued ILOSTAT progress
decisions.description: GitHub Actions confirmed the second WID new-country wave successfully collected source-native numerical share data from 20 additional countries (13,532 selected values, source hashes and private backup), bringing observed geographic scope to 63 distinct codes. Overnight ILOSTAT collected 50 more official bulk files with no losses: 1,019 of 1,964 verified. Neither is a claim of integrated canonical coverage.

decisions.title: Prepare third genuinely disjoint WID geographic collection
decisions.description: Retain frozen WID second-wave successful source ID counts, then change the same official-country source downloader to attempt 20 additional candidate countries outside the entire verified 63-country scope. Success will be determined by live numerical source and private checksum receipts, not selected-country planning.
